depicts.m: This freedom to wander at will, food eaten without humiliation, living among noble people, learning whose only fruit is calm, a mind that stirs only gently even when it looks outward for long: I do not know what generous austerity this is the fruit of.
depicts.sa: यदेतत्स्वच्छन्दं विहरणमकार्पण्यमशनं सहार्यैः संवासः श्रुतमुपशमैकव्रतफलम् । मनो मन्दस्पन्दं बहिरपि चिरस्यापि विमृशन् न जाने कस्यैष परिणतिरुदारस्य तपसः ॥
depicts.why: Shows wonder at a simple sufficient life.

depicts.sa: I am glad I was born, glad I suffered so, glad I did make big blunders, glad to enter peace.
depicts.why: Shows gladness for all of it.

depicts.sa: how wonderfully and how hospitably I was received in every country in the West.
depicts.why: Shows a returning traveller giving thanks for kindness abroad.

gloss: Valmiki's Rama is pleased by one kindness and cannot repay Hanuman when he knows what was done for him.

hero.m: Keep a grateful heart and a friendly spirit. Everything grows out of friendship; a friend is the greatest blessing.
hero.sa: कृतज्ञमनसा भाव्यं मित्रभावेन चानघ / मित्रात्प्रभवते सर्वं मित्रं धन्यतरं स्मृतम्

loci.m: Do not speak ill of food; that is a vow. Breath is food, the body eats food; the body rests on breath and breath rests in the body.
loci.sa: अन्नं न निन्द्यात् । तद्व्रतम् । प्राणो वा अन्नम् । शरीरमन्नादम् । प्राणे शरीरं प्रतिष्ठितम् ।

loci.m: A single kindness done to him, however small, was enough to please him; a hundred wrongs he did not keep in mind, being master of himself.
loci.sa: कदाचिदुपकारेण कृतेनैकेन तुष्यति । न स्मरत्यपकाराणां शतमप्यात्मवत्तया॥

practices.m: Whoever offers me with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit or water, that offering of love from the pure-hearted I accept.
practices.sa: पत्रं पुष्पं फलं तोयं यो मे भक्त्या प्रयच्छति । तदहं भक्त्युपहृतमश्नामि प्रयतात्मनः ॥
practices.why: Shows offering even a little as thanks.

practices.m: Giving in secret, a warm welcome for whoever comes home, silence after doing a kindness, speaking in public of kindness received, no arrogance in wealth, talking of others without a whiff of contempt: who taught the good this vow, hard as walking a sword's edge?
practices.sa: प्रदानं प्रच्छन्नं गृहमुपगते सम्भ्रमविधिः प्रियं कृत्वा मौनं सदसि कथनं चाप्युपकृते । अनुत्सेको लक्ष्म्यामनभिभवगन्धाः परकथाः सतां केनोद्दिष्टं विषममसिधाराव्रतमिदम् ॥
practices.why: Shows speaking openly of help received.

practices.m: Keep a grateful heart and a friendly spirit. Everything grows out of friendship; a friend is the greatest blessing.
practices.sa: कृतज्ञमनसा भाव्यं मित्रभावेन चानघ / मित्रात्प्रभवते सर्वं मित्रं धन्यतरं स्मृतम्
practices.why: Names gratitude as the disposition to hold.

practices.m: Do not neglect your duties to the gods and the ancestors. Let your mother be a god to you. Let your father be a god to you. Let your teacher be a god to you. Let your guest be a god to you.
practices.sa: देवपितृकार्याभ्यां न प्रमदितव्यम् । मातृदेवो भव । पितृदेवो भव । आचार्यदेवो भव । अतिथिदेवो भव ।
practices.why: Shows those who raised and taught you are to be honoured as one honours a deity.

practices.m: Whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you offer, whatever you give, whatever austerity you practise, Kaunteya, do it as an offering to me.
practices.sa: यत्करोषि यदश्नासि यज्जुहोषि ददासि यत् । यत्तपस्यसि कौन्तेय तत्कुरुष्व मदर्पणम् ॥
practices.why: Shows each meal and gift handed back.

practices.m: Honouring one's mother, father and teachers is, I think, the highest duty. One who lives this way wins the worlds and great renown.
practices.sa: मातापित्रोर्गुरूणां च पूजा बहुमता मम / अत्र वर्तन्नरो लोकान्यशश्च महदश्नुते
practices.why: Cultivates reverence toward those who raised and taught one.

practices.m: Don't sleep past sunrise. On rising, first greet your mother and father, and your teacher or another elder; that is how a long life is won.
practices.sa: न चाभ्युदितसायी स्यात्प्रायश्चित्ती तथा भवेत् / मातापितरमुत्थाय पूर्वमेवाभिवादयेत् / आचार्यमथवाऽप्यन्तं तथाऽऽयुर्विदन्ते महत्
practices.why: Shows a daily act of respect to parents.

practices.m: By housing people and giving them food, he becomes a world for people. By finding grass and water for animals, he becomes a world for animals. When beasts, birds and even ants live off his house, he becomes a world for them.
practices.sa: यन्मनुष्यान्वासयते यदेभ्योऽशनं ददाति तेन मनुष्याणामथ यत्पशुभ्यस्तृणोदकं विन्दति तेन पशूनां यदस्य गृहेषु श्वापदा वयाꣳस्या पिपीलिकाभ्य उपजीवन्ति तेन तेषां लोको
practices.why: Shows a household is seen as something many lives rest on.

stories.l: Where you start is not where you end; you can be taken in from nothing.
stories.s: Across his later works Tulsidas tells his own story: left by his parents at birth, he wandered door to door for scraps, no job, no trade, no skill, ignored by everyone. Good people told him not to worry; Hanuman raised him like a child; Ram's name, he says, turned a thorny babul into a mango tree. Even when he went astray, he was taken back.
stories.t: Tulsidas, the boy who begged for scraps

stories.l: Strength without humility is blind. The one blocking your path may be family.
stories.s: Searching for a flower for Draupadi, mighty Bhima finds an old monkey blocking the path and orders it to move. Told to lift its tail himself, he cannot budge it. The monkey is his elder brother Hanuman, who embraces him and teaches him.

stories.l: Loyalty means staying through the bad season, not only the good.
stories.s: A hunter's poisoned arrow withers the tree where a parrot has always lived. The parrot refuses to leave it. Indra, moved by its loyalty, restores the tree.
stories.t: The parrot who stayed with the withered tree

stories.l: Friendships made in hard times deserve to be kept; say so out loud.
stories.s: After six happy months, Ram sends his monkey and bear friends home with gifts. Angad, whose father is dead, begs to stay: Ram is his father and mother now. Ram embraces him and sends him on. To the boatman Guha he says: you are a brother to me; keep visiting.
stories.t: Ram says goodbye to his friends
